sections.title: Greeting
sections.line: Paul writes as an apostle by God's will, not his own.

sections.title: Chosen before the foundation
sections.line: Election stated as praise rather than posed as a problem.

sections.title: Redemption and the disclosed plan
sections.line: Blood-bought forgiveness reveals a plan to unite everything in Christ.

sections.title: Sealed and guaranteed
sections.line: The Spirit is the deposit on an inheritance not yet paid.

sections.title: A prayer for sight
sections.line: Not for more gifts, but for eyes to see these.

themes.note: Every blessing is located in him, never merely alongside him.
Each gift traced to God's purpose, never to our merit.

themes.theme: To the praise of his glory
themes.note: The refrain closing each movement, naming the point.
Resurrection power is the measure of what works in believers.

references.why: Humanity's mandate over creation is claimed for Christ, so the church's head already rules everything under his feet.

purpose.statement: Paul wants us to know our standing was settled before the world began, so that nothing happening later can unsettle it.
He wants us to believe God has one plan — to gather everything into Christ — so that our own salvation reads as part of it.
He prays for enlightened eyes rather than new gifts, because what the Ephesians lack is not provision but sight of what they hold.
